content: Rifapentine is a rifamycin antibiotic used in combination with other medications to treat active tuberculosis (TB) of the lungs. It may also be used with isoniazid to prevent active TB infections in individuals who are infected with the bacteria, such as those with a positive TB skin test. This antibiotic is effective only against bacterial infections and does not work for viral infections like the common cold or flu. How to Use: Rifapentine should be taken orally with food as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice weekly. For optimal effectiveness, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, take it on the same day(s) of the week and at the same time each day. Continue taking this medication, along with other TB medications, for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve. Side Effects: Common side effects include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, and headache. Rifapentine may cause harmless reddish discoloration of urine, sweat, saliva, or tears, which will resolve after stopping the medication. Rarely, it may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during or months after treatment. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. Precautions: Before taking rifapentine, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other rifamycins (e.g., rifampin), or any other substances. Alcohol use may increase the risk of liver disease. Rifapentine may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it may increase the risk of bleeding in both the mother and infant if taken in the last weeks of pregnancy. It is unknown if rifapentine passes into breast milk, but similar drugs do. Monitor infants exposed through breast milk for signs of liver toxicity, such as irritability, prolonged crying, yellowing of the eyes, appetite loss, vomiting, or changes in urine or stool color. Drug Interactions: Rifapentine can accelerate the removal of other medications from the body, potentially reducing their effectiveness. It may also decrease the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods (e.g., pills, patches, rings), increasing the risk of pregnancy. Discuss reliable backup birth control methods with your doctor. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as folate and vitamin B12 levels, potentially causing false results. Overdose: In case of overdose with serious symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. Storage: Store rifapentine at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed. Important Notes: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about rifapentine. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
